newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to oversee shaping of Russia's 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to oversee shaping of Russia's 1998 budget.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin confirmed on Wednesday he would personally oversee the preparation of Russia's 1998 budget because of problems drawing up the 1997 spending plan.

The government has already approved moves to cut spending in its 1997 budget by one-fifth because of a shortfall of revenues which has shown the inadequacies of the original plan adopted by parliament and signed by the president.

"It became obvious at the start of the year that it (the 1997 budget) is unrealistic on a series of important points," Yeltsin said in a message to the Federation Council, the upper house of parliament, released by the presidential press service.
"I repeat that I will not allow such a practice to happen again. I am taking the preparation of a realistic federal budget for 1998 under my control."
Yeltsin said in a radio address on February 28 that he had signed the original 1997 budget only with misgivings to avoid social unrest and he would take personal charge of the 1998 bill.
He did not make clear how precisely he would increase his role in drawing up the budget.

The government was forced into action by the 1997 budget law which states that it must present a bill on sequestering, or cutting spending, to the lower house of parliament if revenues in any quarter are below 90 percent of planned levels.
Revenues were less than 60 percent of budgeted levels for the first quarter of this year.
The lower house, the State Duma, is dominated by communists and nationalists who have threatened to oppose the cuts.
Yegor Stroyev, the chairman of the Federation Council upper house, was quoted by Prime-Tass news agency last week as saying his chamber also opposed budget spending cuts.
